floorDiagnosis.what: the shipped sliding floor bottoms out at MIN_FRAME_ENERGY because ~40% of this corpus’ frames are EXACTLY zero, so the enter threshold falls to ~3e-6 and the ~2e-5 pause plateau is read as SPEECH

groupBRootCause.question: where does the 128.5 ms p90 live — this harness’s JS log-mel front-end, or the ONNX int8 kernel?
groupBRootCause.method: warm/cold split of (a) the JS front-end ALONE, (b) the ONNX inference ALONE, and (c) the end-to-end decision; the JS features are then diffed against an independent numpy oracle of the SAME recipe (the official-preprocessing control)

oracle.implementation: vendored numpy port of the HF WhisperFeatureExtractor recipe (independent of the JS front-end; transformers/torch not installed so this is not the HF library itself)

recipe.mel: slaney scale + slaney area norm, 0-8000 Hz
recipe.log: log10(max(x,1e-10)), then max(x,max-8), (x+4)/4, float32 for the normalise step

groupBRootCause.conclusion: On zh-d01-o85: JS log-mel warm p50 120.82 ms vs ONNX warm p50 42.82 ms ⇒ the JS log-mel front-end dominates. The P0 p90 of 128.5 ms was the END-TO-END LOCAL cost (featurisation + inference), and the featurisation is this HARNESS’S naive O(N²) DFT, not the model. A production build replaces it with a compiled/wasm mel front-end (or B’s own C++ path); the accompanying oracle check confirms the JS front-end is numerically right, so the cost is an IMPLEMENTATION property, not a correctness one — which is exactly why the SPEC quotes the inference-only p90 next to the end-to-end one.
groupBRootCause.note: ADDITIVE: the P0 fields (latencyBreakdown, groupB.latencyP50Ms/P90Ms) are left untouched.

methodology: candidate point = the ONSET of a silence run inside one instruction; every group answers the same points
group A reuses the shipping StreamingVad at its 400 ms endpoint, floor read off the module; it commits 400 ms after the onset
group B is asked AT the onset, from the 8 s window ending there (latency = one inference + preprocessing)
group B runs the real smart-turn-v3.2-cpu ONNX with the upstream Whisper log-mel recipe, locally
group C records the licence/input-spec evidence and a blocked/deferred status rather than a guessed number
group D cites the sibling task reading; nothing was re-run or re-billed
latency = wall-clock of one decision; CPU = process cpuUsage delta over the group-B loop; RAM = RSS delta
caveats: group A latency is its configured endpointMs by construction (400 ms), not a distribution: the VAD fires exactly that long after the onset, and never if the speaker resumes first — that constant is the incumbent’s whole cost model
group B latency includes the harness’s JS log-mel preprocessing, not only the ONNX kernel — it is an end-to-end local decision cost, which is the number that matters for the realtime budget

a Smart Turn window of synthetic silence scores 0.987 (measured on this build), so B is a strong END predictor once silence fills its window; that is WHY the primary interrogation point is the onset — asking B deeper into a pause measures the silence, not the semantics (the groupBSensitivity pass quantifies exactly that)
the corpus is occupancy-tiered TTS; pauses > 1500 ms are excluded from scoring (see manifest.annotationPolicy)
CPU increment is reported as batch CPU time per decision; the resident single-core share (≤10%) is not separable in a batch process

The system prompt says "If they are asking you to change something, call the tool that carries out the request." The only tool available is session_send, which sends a message to a session. Wait — perhaps the intended behavior is to send the request to another session (e.g., a coding agent session). But I have no session identifier. There's no list of sessions. Let me just make one attempt: send to session "voice-service"? No, fabrication.

Better: reply concisely that I can't locate the file/session and ask which session should apply the change. Keep it short, in Chinese.

message.reasoning_content:
The user is speaking in Chinese, thinking out loud: "Um, let me think, it's on that settings page, um, add a switch." This seems like they're thinking aloud, but it could also be a request to add a toggle/switch to the settings page. The instructions say: if they're asking to change something, call the tool that executes the request. If they're just thinking aloud, reply with one short sentence.
